heroHeadline: Iran Halts US Talks — Demands Israeli Withdrawal From Lebanon; Threatens Full Hormuz Closure; Oil Surges 7%; Sgt. Tyukin Killed — Day 94
heroSubtitle: Day 94 (June 1, 2026): Iran's state outlet Tasnim announced that Iranian negotiators would halt all message exchanges with the US through intermediaries — 'no dialogue will take place' until Israel withdraws from Lebanon and stops attacks in Lebanon and Gaza. Iran simultaneously threatened to 'completely block the Strait of Hormuz and activate other fronts including the Bab al-Mandeb Strait,' sending Brent crude surging ~7% to approximately $97/bbl. The announcement directly linked the nuclear/Hormuz diplomatic track to the Lebanon military campaign for the first time, placing the June 2–3 Doha round 4 in serious doubt. On the Lebanon front: IDF strikes killed 12+ Lebanese across Nabatieh, Tyre, and the Litani River zone on Day 94. IDF Staff Sgt. Michael Tyukin, 21, of the Givati Brigade Reconnaissance Unit, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone near Beaufort Castle — 4 soldiers lightly wounded; Tyukin had emigrated from Ukraine in 2020. A Hezbollah FPV drone struck near Rosh Hanikra, wounding 3 Israeli civilians; IDF Northern Command declared the entire Rosh Hanikra–Achziv coastline a closed military zone. Lebanon's cumulative toll reached approximately 3,162+ killed. In the Strait of Hormuz, the dual-lane navigation system solidified: IRGC confirmed 15 vessels (including 4 oil tankers) transited under IRGC authorization in the prior 24 hours, as Fortune documented the competing US 'guidance' route along Oman's coast. Israel's Defense Minister Katz stated forces would remain at Beaufort Castle 'as part of the security zone in Lebanon.'
